Analysis: Hypothesis 1 is highly innovative with a multi-component approach that leverages CRISPRa, nanoparticle delivery, iron chelation, and autophagy modulation to enhance glutathione synthesis; however, its complexity can hinder mechanistic clarity, make preclinical testing challenging, and raise compounded safety concerns. Hypothesis 2, while also novel, takes a more streamlined approach by focusing on dual gene therapy to modulate mitochondrial iron via mitoNEET and boost antioxidant defense through system Xc⁻ upregulation. This strategy, though not free of its own risks (such as potential off-target effects with CRISPR-based activation and viral vector concerns), offers a more directly testable hypothesis with clearer mechanistic pathways and a potentially better safety profile due to its reduced complexity.
